transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-03-25
Start: 15:00 PT
Duration: 42m
Attendees: Sam (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Mark (Rivermark Eng), Jess (Rivermark PM), Liam (Rivermark SRE)

Summary: quick review of last week's benchmark, tune streaming settings, agree next tests.

[00:00] Sam (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call, you all good?
[00:08] Mark (Rivermark): Yep, here. Sorry running a little late, laptop update.
[00:12] Jess (Rivermark): I'm on.
[00:14] Priya (Redwood SE): Morning — or afternoon — all, ready to dive into the TTFT numbers.
[00:20] Liam (Rivermark): Ready.

[01:05] Sam: Last week we switched from full response to streaming and saw TTFT drop from about 240ms median to roughly 125ms. Priya, can you confirm which kernel you used for that run?
[01:18] Priya: Yeah, that run used the optimized fused-attn kernel on the A100 pool with int8 quant, kv cache enabled. The streaming path also turned on small-chunk flushing at 64 tokens which reduced initial chunking overhead.
[01:32] Mark: Right, we noticed the improvement, but tails were still spiky during peak bursts. Our SLO is 150ms p50 and p95 350ms, so we're under p50 but worried about p95.

[02:10] Priya: For the p95 we looked at two sources: batching delay and sequence-length tails. When a few long sequences intersperse, they block batching for the slot. We recommended prefix-trimming and early KV cache warm.
[02:28] Jess: Quick question — you mentioned warm prefix, can you explain how that works in streaming?
[02:34] Priya: Sure. Warm prefix means we pre-populate the kv cache by sending the prompt up to the point where generation starts but not waiting for the full response. It costs a tiny bit of compute but cuts the first token time because the heavy attention matmuls are already in cache.

[04:00] Sam: We also suggested a hybrid: for requests under 128 tokens use the low-latency path with small batching; above that, route to a throughput pool. That might help p95 without raising cost too much.
[04:20] Mark: Do you have numbers on that split? Our traffic is like 70% <64 tokens, 20% 64-256, 10% >256.
[04:29] Priya: With your distribution, the hybrid routing should capture most requests on the low-latency group. In our test, splitting at 128 reduced overall p95 by ~80ms for this mix, with a marginal cost bump of ~6%.

[06:00] Liam: What about kernel choices — you used fused-attn. Is that stable for our larger seqs? We had some memory jitter last week hitting 512 tokens.
[06:12] Priya: Good callout. Fused-attn is great for 128-512 in many cases, but on 512+ it can run into fragmentation on smaller GPU configs. The fallback is baseline kernel which is slightly slower but more consistent memory usage. We can toggle per-route.
[06:28] Mark: So we could use fused for <384 and baseline for >=384?
[06:32] Priya: Exactly. Also quantization: int8 gave good perf but sometimes adds a few ms to p50 on cold starts — we saw faster steady-state but a small TTFT penalty if the kernel isn't JIT warmed.

[08:10] Sam: A pragmatic next step: Priya will run a streaming TTFT test with a 128-token warm prefix and fused-attn on the low-latency pool, baseline on the high-throughput pool, and capture p50/p95/p99 and tail events.
[08:28] Priya: I'll capture both raw token-level timestamps and aggregated metrics so we can see where time is spent — kernel, serialization, network, batching.

[09:15] Jess: Anything else about batching? We use bursty patterns during morning opening hours, which seems to create big batches and some stalls.
[09:24] Priya: For bursty traffic we recommended adaptive max_batch_ms downramp — reduce max_batch_ms under load so small requests don't wait. Also enable per-customer prefix cache to avoid recomputing.
[09:40] Mark: How invasive is per-customer prefix cache for us? Security or data residency concerns?
[09:46] Sam: The prefix cache lives in customer-owned VPC in your case, and data is encrypted at rest. This is an opt-in config; from a compliance standpoint we can mirror logs to your audit stream.

[11:00] Liam: On the topic of streaming chunk size: you mentioned 64 earlier. Is 64 recommended or could 32 help TTFT more?
[11:10] Priya: 32 reduces first-chunk latency at the cost of more RPCs and slightly higher token overhead. In our tests, 64 is a good sweet spot for most models. For very tight TTFT targets <100ms we sometimes push 32 but watch for CPU/RPC pressure.

[13:00] Mark: What's the effort to flip the kernel toggle per route? We'd like to try the fused-to-baseline rule for a day on a canary subset.
[13:10] Priya: It's a config change on the rollout policy in Console; we can do a canary with 5% traffic to start. Takes minutes to change, then we monitor. We'll also supply a script to revert if tails worsen.

[15:20] Sam: We ran a quick canary earlier today internally; p50 dropped 30ms but p99 had a small bump until the cache warmed. We think scheduling a warm-up window before peak helps.
[15:35] Jess: Warm-up window meaning run a replay of traces?
[15:40] Priya: Yup — replay a 5-10 minute sample of production traffic to pre-warm caches. Mark, you mentioned you can share an hour of traffic — that will be great.

[17:00] Mark: I can export an hour from last week, obfuscated, and drop it into the S3 bucket you shared. Is CSV enough?
[17:08] Priya: JSONL with timestamps is easiest, but CSV with prompt and timestamp fields is okay; we'll convert. Please include sequence lengths.

[18:40] Liam: Any risks with quantization and our compliance requirements? We need to ensure determinism for audits.
[18:48] Sam: Quantization doesn't change logs or inputs; outputs can differ slightly but we can run golden set evals. For audit determinism we keep golden-model runs on baseline float32. We also provide regression alerts tied to prompt sets.

[20:10] Jess: On the cost side, what's the expected delta when enabling the hybrid routing and fused-attn?
[20:20] Priya: For your token mix, we estimate 4-8% higher compute cost versus baseline but with ~25-40% latency improvement on p50/p95 depending on routing thresholds. We can tighten the split to trade cost vs latency.

[22:00] Mark: Can Redwood share the benchmark config you used so we can replicate?
[22:08] Sam: Yes — I'll send the config and the exact kernel flags. Also we'll include the script to collect token-level timestamps from your side for correlation.

[24:15] Priya: Implementation notes: 1) enable streaming path with chunk size 64, 2) set warm_prefix=128 for warm-up run, 3) per-route kernel policy: fused for seq<384 else baseline, 4) enable adaptive max_batch_ms with low-latency tier at 8ms, throughput tier at 60ms.

[26:30] Jess: Sounds good. For success criteria, can we propose: p50 < 120ms, p95 < 300ms, errors < 0.1% over a 24h window?
[26:45] Sam: That seems reasonable as a pilot target. We'll validate after the next benchmark run.

[28:00] Mark: One more question — when you say kernel fallback, is that per-request or per-batch?
[28:08] Priya: It's per-request routing; the system routes requests before batching so the batch will be fairly homogeneous. For mixed batches we have safety fallbacks to avoid hangs.

[30:00] Liam: Any logging changes we should expect? More token-level logs or increased trace volume?
[30:08] Sam: We'll add a token-timing trace for the pilot; counts are moderate but we can dial retention. Audit logs will include kernel and route metadata.

[32:40] Priya: Quick note — we saw a small bug in the fused-attn on one older CUDA microcode that caused a rare OOM. We flagged it and it's fixed in the runtime build we'll include in the config. If your infra is older, we'll pick the safe baseline until you patch.

[34:10] Mark: I'll check our infra versions and align with Liam.

[34:16] Liam: I'll send the CUDA and driver versions in the ticket.

[35:00] Sam: Recap of next steps: Sam to send configs and kernel notes; Priya runs the streaming TTFT tests and posts logs; Mark shares traffic trace and infra versions; Jess confirms success criteria. We'll schedule the deep-dive next week.

[36:10] Jess: Can we get the canary timeline? If tests go well, we aim to roll to 25% by next Tuesday.

[36:20] Sam: Sounds doable. We'll aim for that and flag any regressions.

[38:00] Mark: One small ask — can you include cost delta estimates per route in the config email so finance can eyeball?

[38:08] Sam: Yep, will include a simple delta table.

[40:00] Priya: I'll also attach the raw token timing CSV so you can ingest into your dashboards.

[41:10] Sam: Great — thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the artifacts.

[41:15] Jess: Thanks, bye.
[41:17] Mark: Thanks.
[41:20] Liam: Bye.
